description: Maya found tarot through TikTok and now pulls a card every morning with her coffee. As a designer she cares as much about the deck art as the meanings, and she often shares her draws to her Instagram stories.
Denise works 12-hour ICU shifts and uses a three-card spread afterward to sort through what she's carrying. She doesn't take the cards literally; for her it works like journaling with prompts.

Javier started using the app after his marriage ended and keeps asking variations of the same relationship question. He tends to re-draw until he gets an answer he likes, and he'd never admit how often he opens it.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Structured reflection and interest in symbolism

description: Priya is a skeptic who finds the symbolism genuinely interesting and uses tarot to break out of overthinking. She reads card meanings the way she reads technical documentation, thoroughly and critically.
Rosalind has read physical cards for 30 years and uses the app as a reference and a travel deck. She is quietly critical of apps that oversimplify card meanings.
Kai pulls cards with friends in the dorm, half as entertainment and half sincerely. Tarot overlaps with their interest in astrology and witchy aesthetics.

demographics.profession: Owner of a candle and crystal shop

description: Tasha runs a small metaphysical shop and sometimes offers readings to customers. She uses the app to practice and to learn new decks before stocking them.
Brendan uses random draws as creative prompts for characters and plot twists, a trick borrowed from novelists who have done it for decades. He has no interest in the mystical side.

demographics.profession: PhD candidate and graduate research assistant

description: Lucia is stressed about her dissertation, her funding, and whether academia is worth it. She tells herself tarot is just reflection, but she notices which cards keep repeating.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Comfort and ritual after losing her husband

description: Grace's daughter installed the app for her after her husband died. She finds comfort in the ritual and the gentle, hopeful language, and avoids anything that sounds ominous.
Dev sleeps about four hours a night and uses a single-card pull to check in with his own mood before it spills over onto patients. Speed matters more to him than depth.
Hannah pulls a card before auditions to get into a confident headspace. She knows it's partly superstition and doesn't mind.
Marcus started during a layoff scare and found the ritual calming. Nobody at work knows, and he wants to keep it that way.
Yuki collects digital decks the way other people collect sneakers. She studies how different artists reinterpret the same card.
Carol uses tarot imagery in her own reflective practice and never with patients. She is interested in archetypes and their overlap with religious symbolism.
Tyler's girlfriend got him into tarot, and now he pulls cards before big pitches. He calls them strategic thinking prompts when his friends ask.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Processing her own reactions to sessions

description: Aaliyah uses tarot privately to process her reactions to difficult sessions, and keeps it strictly separate from her clinical work.
Frank's granddaughter showed him the app, and now he reads the card history like trivia. He enjoyed learning that tarot began as a card game in 15th-century Italy.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A moment for herself after bedtime

description: Sofia is a single mom with ten quiet minutes after her kids are asleep, and a reading is her one moment just for herself. She often asks about money and her children's futures.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Part of a broader spiritual practice

description: For River, tarot sits alongside moon cycles and meditation in a broader spiritual practice. They want a community of other readers.

demographics.race_ethnicity: Middle Eastern or North African (Lebanese American)

description: Nadia treats tarot as a randomized prompt generator for introspection. As a scientist she is slightly embarrassed by how much she enjoys it.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Started as UX research and stayed

description: Owen first studied tarot apps for UX inspiration and ended up using one himself. He appreciates good randomization and well-made animations.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Nostalgia for her grandmother's card readings

description: Gloria grew up around her grandmother's Spanish-deck card readings, and the app feels nostalgic. She is skeptical of new-age packaging.
Liam is eighteen months sober and uses a daily card as a reflection tool next to his recovery readings. He is careful not to let it replace his sponsor or his meetings.
Bethany was raised in a megachurch and is exploring spirituality outside it. Opening the app feels a little rebellious, and she has mixed feelings about it.

demographics.race_ethnicity: Middle Eastern or North African (Egyptian American)

description: Ahmed pulls a card while waiting between fares, mostly out of boredom, and it has become a habit. He likes the short daily messages.
Jenna does readings for bridesmaids at bachelorette parties and uses the app to prep. For her, tarot is a social activity first.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Teaching archetypes and the hero's journey

description: Theo uses the major arcana to teach archetypes and the hero's journey alongside literature units. He appreciates the Fool's journey as a narrative structure.

desired_features: No predictions about pregnancy or health

description: Mei is in a hard, uncertain season of IVF and finds the ritual soothing during the two-week waits. She is careful not to read too much into any single draw.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Companionship and reflection on the road

description: Rick picked up tarot from a podcast on long drives along I-80. He is surprisingly deep into the symbolism and relates to the solitude of The Hermit.
Chloe moved across the country for a job and doesn't know anyone yet. A nightly card is a small piece of company.
Gabe is in recovery from a gambling habit and is wary of anything that feels like chance. He chose this app carefully because it avoids gamified rewards.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Reflecting on belonging as a new citizen

description: Ifeoma recently became a U.S. citizen and is building a new sense of identity. She uses readings to reflect on belonging.
Paul is newly retired and trying to figure out who he is without a job title. He finds The Fool card weirdly relevant.

demographics.profession: Retail associate and community college student

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A sense of guidance after aging out of foster care

description: Destiny recently aged out of foster care and craves guidance she never had. She uses the app often, which is why supportive, grounded language matters.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A private space while coming out

description: Sam recently came out and is still telling people. The readings are a private space to process something that is still unfolding.
Lauren is separating from her husband and uses readings to process grief without burdening her friends.
Kwame is a first-generation college graduate facing big career decisions without a family roadmap. He uses spreads to lay out his options.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A new daily ritual as an empty nester

description: Ingrid's youngest just left for college, and the quiet house prompted a new daily habit.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Structure during the move to civilian life

description: Ray left the Army and is adjusting to civilian work. He's skeptical of tarot but values the structure of a daily routine.
Elena uses cards privately to generate conversation starters for her own coaching practice and personal reflection.
Jordan uses random draws to break creative blocks during brainstorming sessions at work.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Managing client sessions and practicing decks

description: Marisol reads tarot professionally and uses the app to track client sessions and practice with new decks.
Noah studies the app professionally and kept using it because he likes it. He pays close attention to how the app handles user data.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Exploring imagery for her own practice

description: Beatrice explores tarot imagery for her own creative practice and keeps a strict line between that and her clients.
Victor draws cards to shake up stuck second acts and to rethink characters' motivations.
Anjali does a quarterly retro spread as a personal planning ritual, then compares it against the previous quarter.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A weekly segment on his show

description: Curtis pulls a card live on his show each week and riffs on it with his co-host.
Wren studies card iconography for client tattoo designs and has started reading for herself along the way.
Malik uses spreads as journaling prompts in the workshops he runs, framed as reflection exercises rather than predictions.
Iris draws cards to build character backstories for the fantasy novel she writes between bookstore shifts.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Plot twists for his D&D campaign

description: Hector runs a weekly Dungeons and Dragons campaign and uses tarot for NPC fortunes and plot twists at the table.
Penelope owns forty physical decks and wants digital versions too. She likes comparing how each deck handles the same card.
Arturo is an amateur historian fascinated by tarot's Renaissance origins and its later esoteric history.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Reference while designing her own deck

description: Zoe is designing her own deck for a class project and studies existing decks for reference.
Felix uses card imagery to spark themes for songs when he's stuck.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A weekly poem from a single draw

description: Rachel writes one poem a week based on a single draw and keeps a record of every card she's written from.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Studying tarot mechanics for a card game

description: Dmitri is studying tarot's structure and mechanics for a card-based video game he's designing.
Luna makes tarot-inspired jewelry and uses the app to get the symbolism right.
Simone is designing a quilt series based on the major arcana and studies each card's colors and composition.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Feeling close to his late wife

description: Bill's late wife read tarot, and using the app makes him feel close to her.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Something gentle to do on flare days

description: Tamara lives with a chronic illness. On flare days, a reading is something gentle she can do from bed.
Ethan is anxious during his company's fundraising round and uses readings as a pressure valve.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Five minutes for herself while caregiving

description: Grace-Ann cares for her mother while raising a teenager. A single card is her five minutes to herself.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Reframing setbacks during a job search

description: Omar was laid off from a tech job and has found the search demoralizing. Readings help him reframe setbacks.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Late-night company while feeding her baby

description: Kelsey is postpartum and sleep-deprived, and pulls cards during late-night feedings.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Comfort that began during cancer treatment

description: Harold found unexpected comfort in the ritual during cancer treatment and kept going after he recovered.
Jasmine manages anxiety and uses readings alongside therapy, not instead of it.
Luis runs a small farm outside Fresno. In a drought year full of financial worry, the ritual steadies him.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Processing the loss of her dog

description: Morgan's dog died last month, and she reads cards about grief and memory.
Brianna does group readings at sorority events. It's entertainment first, with the occasional surprisingly real moment.
Diego does tarot readings for his chat between games, and the segment has become a fan favorite.
Ashley and her partner Tom do relationship check-in spreads together on date night. It gets them talking about things they'd otherwise skip.
notes: Uses the app jointly with partner Tom Reilly, 32.

description: Ruth reads cards for her bridge club as a fun twist on their weekly game, and her grandchildren call her Grandma Ruth the oracle.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Readings for regulars on slow nights

description: Nate reads for regulars on slow nights, which has turned into a bit of a bar tradition.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Discussion fodder for her book club

description: Priyanka hosts a book club and pulls a card for each novel's protagonist to spark discussion.

demographics.profession: High school senior and fast-food crew member

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Curiosity because his friends do it

description: Cody started because his friends were doing it and found it more interesting than he expected.
Fiona leads historical tours in Salem and treats October as tarot season every year.
Jamal uses absurd draws as material for comedy bits.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: A monthly ritual with her sisters

description: Ann and her two sisters, who live in other states, do a sister spread together over video call every month.
notes: Reads jointly with her two sisters over video call.

description: Aurora is a yoga instructor for whom tarot is part of a broader holistic practice.
Esperanza blends tarot with healing traditions passed down in her family.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Part of a seasonal pagan practice

description: Rowan is a practicing pagan, and tarot sits alongside the wheel of the year in their practice.
Desmond is exploring his family's Southern folk traditions and is especially interested in their history.
Sienna is an astrology devotee who cross-references her cards with current transits.
Matteo got curious about tarot after learning about its Italian roots and enjoys the historical decks most.
Hazel was raised Quaker and treats the cards as a focus for silent reflection, not divination.

demographics.race_ethnicity: Middle Eastern or North African (Lebanese American)

description: Tariq loves Sufi poetry and enjoys tracing parallels between its imagery and the cards' symbolism.
Juniper pairs her card pulls with a daily tea ritual.

desired_features: Thoth and Marseille decks, not just Rider-Waite-Smith

description: Celeste has been reading since the 1970s and is skeptical of apps that only offer one deck tradition.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Research interest that became a habit

description: Alan researches projective techniques and, somewhat ironically, got hooked on daily draws himself.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Testing whether the shuffle is truly random

description: Brooke logs every draw to test whether the app's shuffle is truly random, and has kept drawing well after the experiment ended.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Took a dare from his wife

description: Gary's wife dared him to try tarot. He now pulls a card daily but won't admit he likes it.

tarot_profile.primary_motivation: Reporting on wellness apps, then personal use

description: Lena started using the app while reporting a story on the wellness-app boom and stayed on as a user.
Isaac is interested in tarot as a case study in how people make meaning from chance.
Pat uses the app purely for fun and never asks it serious questions.
Xavier studies tarot for the cold-reading segment of his stage act.
Monica left evangelical Christianity and is cautiously exploring other spiritual ideas, with some lingering guilt.
Aiden is traveling through Europe on a gap year and pulls a card before choosing his next city.

desired_features: Readings that synthesize the whole spread

description: Lucia critiques every reading she gets and then quietly thinks about it all week. She wants spreads with real synthesis rather than ten parallel mini-readings.
